commenti.body:
I watched years and years ago, before Yorgos ventured into English-language films. It left an impact on me, and I totally understand why a project like this would put him on the map as an interesting director to work with. And clearly there's a consistent (tonally, thematically) with his posterior films.

I admit I was shocked when it got a Best Foreign Language Film nomination at the Oscars though, because Dogtooth goes all the way; it even feature sexually explicit images and incest.

Just watched Killing of a Sacred Deer for the first time, and I'm even more grateful that Dogtooth resonated with people.

I do love the Midnight in Paris take on Nostalgia.   Personally I didn't latch on to Tree of Life, because of its tracing the life experiences of a Baby Boomer, and I've seen so many of these over the course of my life (I'm GenX), it severely mitigated my enjoyment of it, though the cinematography was spectacular.  In all cases though, you're milage may vary, so I'm really happy this resonated with the OP so strongly.
I also think both of those films are brilliant. But *The Lobster* felt like a satire trying too hard: "Look! Isn't this sad and absurd? Laugh, dammit!" Would you agree?

My favorite thing about Dogtooth is that ,underneath all of the shock and the weirdness, it's a pretty basic story about teenage rebellion. The fact that all of those disturbing elements are there to tell the story and not just for shock value is really remarkable. In the hands of a lesser filmmaker, much of it would be a distraction.

I hear you. But I think that might be deliberate. It's definitely the funniest of his regardless, mind. His lobster telephone maybe...

Dogtooth is superb. The spooky, surreal, and somewhat sinister, allegory Greece deserved. I honestly don't feel he's topped it yet.

I always thought that underneath it was an allegory for the sociocultural political and economic situation in Greece around the time leading up to its economic collapse. A place in denial, beholden to ancient myths and outdated orthodoxy refusing to confront reality and stunting its potential future in the process. Possibly the first example of Psychedelic Revanchism in film or popular culture I can recall. Brexit, Boris and Trump were soon come follow in reality though...

As the other guy said, I thought the stupidness of it was very deliberated. Yes, it’s forced - but *everything* in the movie is forced, including the acting. I thought it as a brilliant choice that added to the feel and purpose of the film

I love the deliberate stylization of *Dogtooth* and *Sacred Deer*, but I suppose I only think it works in those more sinister cases, while I think it just hampers any comedic intent. Or perhaps satire simply isn't for me.

I watched it when it first came out.  It was one of the first non-English films I ever watched and the first film that made me question my sanity while watching it.  I couldn't believe you could make a movie like that.  Loved it immediately.
That's fair. And I pretty much concur. Surreal satire is an acquired taste and often a little rich for my blood. Like drinking undiluted grenadine right out of the bottle...

Admittedly, I know too little about Greek society to comment with any confidence, but stunting future generations sounds about right. That tragicomic ending is chilling: a self too twisted and underdeveloped ever to be delivered into reality; a stillborn soul imprisoned in the womb.
Teenage rebellion and family dynamics always contain the traits of the larger social situation.
This is what made Beverly Hills 90210 so compelling and metatextual.
I suggest you take a look at the movie which either "inspired" it or it blatantly ripped off:  The Castle Of Purity (1973) by Mexican director Arturo Ripstein.   It's also very good.

It's my favorite of his. I think it's great how the parents teach their children the wrong meanings of words and totally random facts without any special worldview that they want to push, it seems like a fun way to live in a weird way, just making shit up without any service to some greater cause aside from what your mind can come up with.


I get the metaphor for politics etc but i just like the execution itself
Will definitely check that out, thanks for the rec!
